chunks: And ʿAlī عليه السلام, in Kūfah, used to go out every morning and walk through the markets of Kūfah, market by market, while with him was the whip upon his shoulder. It had two ends, and it used to be called al-Sabībah.

He said: He would stand before the people of each market and call out to them: “O company of traders, put al-istikharah first, seek blessing through ease, draw near to the buyers, adorn yourselves with forbearance, keep away from oppression, give justice to the wronged, and do not go near usury.
“And do not diminish the people’s goods, and do not act wickedly in the land as corrupters.”
He said: Then he would go through all the markets of Kūfah, then return and sit for the people.

key_terms.التُّجَّارِ: the traders or merchants being addressed directly
key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury, an unlawful excess in financial dealings
key_terms.السُّهُولَةِ: ease and gentleness in conduct and dealings
key_terms.الِاسْتِخَارَةَ: seeking goodness and divine guidance before undertaking trade
key_terms.الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزَانَ: measure and weight, meaning fairness and accuracy in trade
key_terms.الْمَظْلُومِينَ: those who have been wronged and are to be given justice

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali عليه السلام instruct merchants in the markets of Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the daily practice of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in supervising the markets of Kūfah and personally instructing merchants in ethical conduct. It emphasizes justice, fairness in trade, gentleness, and avoidance of riba, presenting commerce as an area of moral and social responsibility.
